sn55.12:1.7: Unsurprisingly for a practice with such a high mortality rate, the _udayagāmini_ is not attested in Brahmanical texts. It seems to be a misunderstanding of the _udayanīya_, which is a rite that concludes the sacrifice. After bathing (_avabhṛtha_), the sacrificer emerges from the water (_udayanīya_). Bhāradvāja Śrautasūtra 14.25.13 says that after the _udayanīya_, those performing the sacrifice should move away toward the east, north, or according to some, the north-east. The successful completion of the sacrifice would, of course, be expected to win the favors of the gods, so it is only a small stretch to imagine that they would have been promised the gods’ protection and a heavenly rebirth.
